added_failures_note: the reviewed manifest leaves baseline_suite and after_suite null, so the head arm is the reviewed run's own gate-head.log at b0801885 (598 passed, 0 failed, exit 0) and the base arm I measured independently over tests/ids at the reviewed base e1e6ae6c (594 passed, 0 failed, exit 0); both EXIT=0 with zero failing ids, so the run added no failing test. The reviewed run's gate-after-revert.log cannot serve as a base arm: its header names revision e1e6ae6c but it reports 4 passed, while I reproduced the base (base tree plus the new test file) at 3 failed, 1 passed, exit 1, so that log is a head-arm measurement mislabeled with the base revision.
call_sites: imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:1879 (the gate loop that reassigns all_bindings)
imas_codex/ids/validation.py:240 (validate_mapping's all_passed, the same four-field predicate)
imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:1899 (the corrections 'failed' count, the same four-field predicate)

findings.text: follow-on: the four-field predicate (source_exists and target_exists and transform_executes and units_compatible) is now spelled a third time — in the new gate (mapping.py:1889-1895) and in the corrections 'failed' count (mapping.py:1899-1906) — where imas_codex/ids/validation.py:240 already owns it as BindingCheck's pass condition; a BindingCheck.passed property beside the dataclass would collapse all three spellings to one and keep them from drifting.

follow-on: the reviewed run ships gate-after-revert.log with the header 'revision: e1e6ae6cd25e14c173ff7193c3dc1903755e1daa (working tree)' and a result of 4 passed, but the base tree cannot pass these tests — reproduced against a pristine base tree (e1e6ae6c plus the new test file): 3 failed, 1 passed, exit 1 — so the log is a head-arm measurement mislabeled with the base revision and should not be read as a base arm.

follow-on (pre-existing, surfaced by this change): the corrections summary appends '{failed} binding(s) failed validation checks' whenever report.all_passed is False, and all_passed is False when duplicate_targets is non-empty even though no four-check failure exists, so a mapping whose only defect is a duplicate target now writes '0 binding(s) failed validation checks' — the count no longer matches the persisted-set gate it summarises.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified the gate consumes report.binding_checks in binding order (imas_codex/ids/validation.py:181 appends one check per binding in the same loop that walks bindings), so index alignment holds; the reviewed change adds no new function, so the three referenced sites are the gate and the two pre-existing spellings of the same predicate.
item_verdicts.diff: Read the single commit against the base: b0801885 adds the gate loop in mapping.py (20 added lines plus comment), the new four-test file, and the evidence fragment; git diff --stat e1e6ae6c..b0801885 reports exactly those three files, 218 insertions, 0 deletions, and nothing else.
item_verdicts.done_when: §26's done-when is a unit test showing a binding with a missing target and one with incompatible units each removed from bindings and present as an escalation naming the failed check, a passing sibling kept, and a negative control that returns every binding and reddens the test; tests/ids/test_validation_gates_persistence.py carries all four assertions and the run's negative-control.log shows 3 failed, 1 passed, exit 1, which I reproduced independently against a pristine base tree.
item_verdicts.goal: §26 asks that a binding failing any of validate_mappings' four checks be removed from the persisted set and carried as an escalation naming the failed check while a passing sibling is kept; mapping.py:1879-1897 pairs each binding with report.binding_checks[index] and keeps it only when the check is absent or all four booleans hold, so a failing binding is dropped and the escalation validate_mapping already emits (one per failing binding, reason = joined failed-check messages) remains the record, and coverage now measures the surviving set.
item_verdicts.manifest: The manifest records commit b0801885, the tests/ids gate (598 passed, 5 skipped, 8 deselected, exit 0), the negative control (3 failed, 1 passed, exit 1) and the escalation evidence_inputs, and honestly leaves baseline_suite/after_suite null rather than inventing an arm; it also ships gate-after-revert.log, which reads as a base-arm result but is not one (see the finding), so the suite delta rests on the base arm I measured independently.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The reviewed node was fenced to imas_codex/ids/mapping.py, tests/ids/test_validation_gates_persistence.py, the evidence fragment and a figures directory; git diff --stat e1e6ae6c..b0801885 reports exactly mapping.py (+22), the test file (+171) and the fragment (+25), with the figures directory untouched and no generated or gitignored file staged.

justifications.durability: The negative control at tests/ids/test_validation_gates_persistence.py reddens three of four tests (exit 1) when the gate is mutated to keep every binding, and I reproduced that red independently against a pristine base tree (3 failed, 1 passed, exit 1), so the removal assertions are load-bearing; each assertion compares the code's output against an independent constant (MISSING_TARGET, UNITS_TARGET, GOOD_TARGET) or a report the test supplies rather than a value it also feeds the code.
justifications.evidence: The gate measures the done-when and its result is recorded — gate-head.log shows 598 passed and exit 0 at b0801885, negative-control.log shows 3 failed and exit 1 with the mutation, and the gate-after-revert reproduction resolves to 3 failed on the true base — and I measured the base arm independently at e1e6ae6c (594 passed, exit 0) because the manifest names no baseline/after arm; the one blemish is gate-after-revert.log, a head-arm result mislabeled with the base revision, which does not undermine the measure but should not be read as the base arm.
justifications.fit: The gate follows the module's list-comprehension idiom and carries a mechanism comment naming the four checks rather than any plan or ticket identifier; the test module docstring explains the mechanism, the symbols are named by what they assert, and the commit uses a conventional subject with a mechanism body and no attribution line.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:1879-1897 implements exactly what §26 names — a binding failing any of the four checks is removed and the escalation validate_mapping already records for it (imas_codex/ids/validation.py:172-179, reason = joined failed-check messages) is what remains as the record — and the passing sibling is kept, with coverage (check_coverage_threshold) now run against the surviving set so it measures what is persisted.
justifications.reuse: The gate reaches the correct existing structures (report.binding_checks from imas_codex/ids/validation.py:181) rather than re-validating, but it spells the four-field pass predicate out a third time beside the two pre-existing spellings (imas_codex/ids/validation.py:240 and mapping.py:1899) instead of adding a BindingCheck.passed helper that would own it once, so a third copy can now drift from the other two.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat e1e6ae6c..b0801885 shows the single commit touches exactly the three declared write paths — one source file, one test file, one evidence fragment — with one purpose, and no generated or gitignored file is staged; the declared figures directory is untouched because the node added no figure.
